passage:
Note to file, quarterly review. After the bad winter, when the biggest client left and salaries came late twice, Aparna stayed and took on extra calls without complaint.

At today's review Rukmini stood in front of the team and said, "I'm grateful. I don't want to treat that as a given." Rukmini's voice cracked, and the paper in Rukmini's hand was not steady. It showed a new share table giving Aparna an equal stake, and a promise to share the accounts every month, good or bad. Aparna looked surprised, then pleased.

Afterwards, at the tea point, Rukmini said, "I felt so relieved when you stayed. I never said it." Aparna answered, "You just did."

Farid, office manager

qa.q: What did Rukmini promise to share every month?
qa.a: Rukmini promised to share the accounts every month, good or bad.

qa.q: How does Rukmini feel about Aparna's loyalty, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Deeply grateful and relieved: Rukmini's voice cracked and the paper was not steady, and later Rukmini said, 'I felt so relieved when you stayed.'

qa.q: How does Rukmini show gratitude beyond words?
qa.a: With a new share table giving Aparna an equal stake, honest monthly account updates and thanks in front of the team.

qa.q: How might Aparna have felt at the review?
qa.a: Surprised at first, then pleased, and after the tea-point conversation probably appreciated.

grounding: A partner who stayed loyal through a rough patch is thanked with fair equity, recognition and honest updates rather than treated as always there.

passage:
Usha: Farhan, you awake?
Farhan: always 😅 what's up
Usha: the bank approved the loan. we're safe.
Farhan: WHAT. Usha!! 🎉
Usha: I know. and I've been thinking about last year
Usha: when the orders stopped, when I couldn't pay you for five months
Usha: you could have walked. you had that offer from the big firm
Farhan: I wasn't going to leave you with 40 half-made lamps lol
Usha: I'm serious. I don't think I ever properly thanked you
Usha: so. thank you. and I want to make your share fair, the way we talked about. let's sit with the CA on Monday
Farhan: you don't have to
Usha: I do. and you're getting named as co-founder on the website, not "team"
Farhan: ok now I'm emotional
Usha: also: monthly numbers meeting, every month, even when they're bad. no surprises for you
Farhan: deal ❤️

qa.q: How many months was Usha unable to pay Farhan?
qa.a: Usha couldn't pay Farhan for five months.

qa.q: What was Usha feeling while writing to Farhan?
qa.a: Usha felt deeply grateful and a little guilty at never having properly thanked Farhan.

qa.q: How did Usha show that gratitude in practical ways?
qa.a: Usha proposed sitting with the CA about a fair share, naming Farhan co-founder on the website, and holding honest monthly numbers meetings.

qa.q: How does Farhan experience Usha's message?
qa.a: Farhan is surprised and moved, admitting to feeling emotional, and happy to be recognised.

grounding: A chat shows a young founder deeply grateful to a partner who stayed loyal through a rough patch, who shows it with fair shares, recognition and honest updates.

passage:
In Maheshwar, Charu and Afreen ran a small handloom unit with six looms in an old house by the ghats. The year the orders stopped, Charu's own family begged her to shut it. Afreen stayed. She sold her gold earrings to pay the weavers for two months and never once mentioned it.

Now, three years later, a Delhi boutique had ordered two hundred saris. Charu stood in the courtyard watching the weavers and felt her throat tighten with gratitude.

She didn't want it to stay a feeling. That evening she brought a signboard painter. The old sign said "Charu Handlooms". The new one said "Charu and Afreen Handlooms".

Afreen came out with chai and stopped. "What is this?"

"What it always should have been. And from next month, we look at the accounts together every Sunday. You'll never have to guess how we're doing."

Afreen didn't say anything. She just put the chai down and hugged her.

qa.q: How many saris did the Delhi boutique order?
qa.a: The boutique ordered two hundred saris.

qa.q: What did Charu feel watching the weavers in the courtyard?
qa.a: Charu felt deeply grateful, her throat tightening at the thought of Afreen's loyalty.

qa.q: How did Charu turn her gratitude into action?
qa.a: She put Afreen's name on the signboard and started weekly shared accounts so Afreen would always get honest updates.

qa.q: How did Afreen feel when she saw the new sign?
qa.a: Afreen was moved and speechless, hugging Charu instead of answering.

grounding: The passage shows a young woman deeply grateful to a partner who stayed loyal through a rough patch, showing it through recognition and honest updates rather than taking loyalty for granted.
